See the formula ↓

How the calculation works

Raw marks = Correct × Marks per correct − Incorrect × Penalty

A worked example

In a 20-question exam, 12 correct answers at 4 marks each earn 48 marks. Five wrong answers lose 5 marks at a penalty of 1 each. The result is 43/80 = 53.75%, with three unanswered questions.

Before you use the result

Question counts must be whole numbers and correct plus incorrect cannot exceed the total. Unanswered questions earn zero and have no penalty. Negative totals are displayed without a zero floor. This is a configurable raw-score calculation, not an official prediction for a named examination.

Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

Can the result be negative?

Yes. If penalties exceed marks earned, the raw score is negative. An exam provider may apply a zero floor or another policy afterward.

Does this account for section-specific penalties?

No. Use separate calculations for sections with different rules, then combine the awarded marks correctly.
